A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MASPOB framework and benchmarks. Text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison. The workflow and prompt material in v1 Appendix C is retained as v2 Appendix D.

before.justification: V1 reports original six-benchmark evaluations, convergence results, workflow and backbone comparisons, and component ablations, including the appendix uncertainty experiment.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds prompt-domain robustness and initialization, embedding, uncertainty-approximation, search-granularity and exploration-coefficient experiments.

M1.justification: V2 introduces optional block-coordinate updates and a diagonal LinUCB variant while retaining the default GNN-plus-LinUCB coordinate-search framework. Its graph-construction description also drops bidirectional-edge augmentation. The expanded warm-up procedure is principally clarification: v1 already specified five pretraining rounds in Appendix A.3.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate HotpotQA, DROP, HumanEval, MBPP, GSM8K and MATH with the same task coverage. More complex workflows were already evaluated in v1. V2's alternative prompt pools and component configurations vary settings within retained coverage.

E2.justification: The main IO, CoT, ReAct, PromptBreeder, Instinct, AFlow and MIPRO comparator set is unchanged. Component-level comparisons newly evaluate diagonal LinUCB and two-agent block-coordinate search against default MASPOB in Tables 12-13. MIPRO-generated prompts in Table 5 are a candidate-pool comparison, not a new optimizer baseline.

E3.justification: The reported GSM8K validation size changes from 100 to 150, and concurrent API calls from 30 to 50. Added studies specify controlled variations such as 1/5/10 warm-up evaluations under a fixed total budget of 50 and exploration coefficients 0.05/0.2/1.0. Core metrics and test sizes remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond retaining the earlier ablations, v2 adds prompt-domain robustness in Table 5 and a substantial sensitivity suite in Appendix C. These test dependence on initialization budget, embedding backbone, full versus diagonal uncertainty, single-agent versus block updates, and exploration strength, addressing several previously untested design choices.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations over three test evaluations and specify random seed 42. The added tables follow this existing practice; no new repeated-optimization protocol, confidence intervals or significance tests are reported.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark and ablation values are retained, but Tables 5 and 10-14 substantially expand the reported findings. For example, MIPRO-generated candidates yield a DROP-MATH average of 70.13 versus 69.67 with the original domain; diagonal LinUCB yields 67.90 versus 69.67 for full LinUCB. These are newly reported configuration comparisons, not same-setting performance gains from v1 to v2.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 replaces the single-head mathematical presentation with explicit K-head definitions, including intermediate-layer concatenation and final-layer averaging in Equations (3)-(6). This is a limited expansion of the formal model specification. The optimization objective and UCB mathematics remain unchanged, and no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the claims of sample-efficient prompt optimization for fixed-topology MAS using a GNN, UCB and coordinate ascent, supported by superior aggregate performance across six benchmarks. Additional robustness evidence and wording changes do not materially redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly distinguishes permitted intra-agent retries from unsupported cross-agent cycles and dynamic routing. It adds interpretations concerning candidate-pool dependence, initialization and exploration balance, embedding quality, and diagonal-UCB and block-search tradeoffs. These qualify and extend the existing coordination explanation without replacing it.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-access link and documents role-preserving, style-controlled prompt generation, random warm-up initialization and multi-head aggregation more explicitly. The settings table corrects UCB type from Neural to Linear, consistent with v1's existing method equations. The extensive agent implementations and optimized prompt listings are retained.

R1.justification: Related work adds Semantic Backpropagation by Wang et al. (2024) and multimodal adversarial-robustness work by Dong et al. (2025). MAPRO remains the closest identified prior work and the overall positioning is retained. Venue/year updates for existing references do not constitute additional research coverage.

P1.justification: V2 edits the abstract opening, expands methodological explanations, rewrites Appendix B, and adds limitations and acknowledgements. A new sensitivity Appendix C shifts the largely unchanged workflow appendix to D. Most introduction, experimental narrative and workflow text remains intact, so this is not a wholesale rewrite.

P2.justification: The visual presentation expands with prompt-domain Table 5 and sensitivity Tables 10-14. Figure 1's search panel is redrawn to separate exploration and exploitation, Figure 2(b) changes to best-first ordering, and the earlier uncertainty-ablation table becomes a compact side-by-side display. Existing plotted findings are retained.

improvement.justification: The added controlled studies strengthen evidence that MASPOB's results are robust to several implementation choices. Clearer initialization and prompt-generation details, a code-access link and explicit workflow limitations improve reproducibility and interpretation. These extend an already substantial empirical evaluation; the unexplained GSM8K split revision leaves a reporting ambiguity, making the net improvement limited.
